decision_titles: Participation in UMass Boston senior needs project ($40K fee)
Board of Health funding for winter warming center
plain_text:
FITCHBURG COUNCIL on AGING 
October 8, 2026 MEETING MINUTES 
 
PRESENT: Todd Goodwin, Joe Byrne, Margaret Padovano, Jim Craigen (left at 2:05 pm), Nancy Donohue, 
Eleanor Zichelle, Debbie Dion, Anne Fitch (1:10 pm), Rev. Annie Belmer (1:23 pm), and Amanda Koeck. 
EXCUSED ABSENCE: George Bourque, Bonnie Hautala, and Tom Hopkins 
 
Goodwin called the meeting to order at 1:01 pm and a QUORUM was present. The meeting took place in 
the Fireplace Room at the Fitchburg Senior Center. 
 
ZOOM MEETING   1:09 pm - 1:42 pm 
The Council on Aging hosted a ZOOM meeting with UMass Boston Center for Social and Demographic 
Research. This research group is based in their Gerontology Department and is led by Director Caitlin E. 
Coyle, PhD. They would use various components to identify the needs of our senior population that is 
living longer, more active lives. Those components include a document review, demographic profile, 
focus groups, and key informant interviews. The interviews include any combination of the mayor, city 
council members, police chief, and fire chief, plus a random mail-based survey of 5,000 city residents 
aged 60+. Coyle’s group would use a holistic approach to report key findings. Their recommendations 
would be aimed at maintaining Fitchburg as a healthy lifelong community that supports aging in place. 
The duration of the project is 9-12 months and Fitchburg’s earliest start date would be March 2027. A 
Q&A section followed the presentation. The COA’s main concerns were the all-inclusive participation fee 
of $40K and our return on investment. Following the conclusion of the ZOOM meeting the COA decided 
to revisit the possibility of our participation in the project at our November 12, 2027, meeting. 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT:  None 
 
MINUTES from the September 10, 2026, meeting were emailed to Board members. Donohue motioned 
and Craigen seconded her motion to approve those minutes. There was no discussion and Donohue’s 
motion received unanimous support. 
 
CHAIRPERSON’S REPORT:  Todd Goodwin 
*There was a brief discussion about replenishing our Sunshine Fund. Goodwin appointed Byrne to serve 
as Sunshine Fund Chair. A donation of $20.00 was suggested. Byrne will begin collecting voluntary 
donations at the November 12, 2026, meeting. 
 
EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR’S REPORT:  Amanda Koeck *Koeck recently met with Stephen Curry, Board of 
Health Director, and Sue Christensen, Outreach and Prevention Coordinator. Their discussion focused on 
using the Senior Center as a warming center during the winter months. Curry and Christensen are 
working on a Memorandum of Agreement that includes funding assistance from the Board of Health’s 
budget. Koeck reported a suggested tiered funding structure based on the number of days/nights the 
Senior Center is used as a winter warming center. That structure suggests $500 for 1-5 days/nights, $1K 
for 6-10 days/nights, and a cap of $1500 for 11+ days/nights of use. Funding assistance from the Board of 
Health would help defray the cost of heat and electricity. The COA Board supports funding assistance 
from the Board of Health. 
 
*Koeck reported that the Elm Street wheelchair ramp has been reset and paved. The completion of that 
project allows for easier building ingress and egress. 
 
Unanimously approved at 11/12/2026 COA meeting.
*Koeck championed the lack of parking surrounding the Senior Center, especially on Wallace Avenue, and 
its detrimental effect on our senior population who wish to access the activities and programs offered to 
our older adults. She is concerned that senior citizens pay for parking passes, but there are very few 
parking options available in the neighborhood. The public library construction workers occupy most of 
those parking spaces for the entire day. Koeck recently emailed the mayor’s office, treasurer’s office, 
parking clerk, public library, and Councilor Andrew Van Hazinga with her concerns. She requested that 
the construction workers park elsewhere during their work day. Koeck has noticed a slight improvement 
in parking availability since that email correspondence. 
 
*Koeck will be attending the MCOA Fall Conference in Southbridge, MA, from October 21-23, 2026. The 
theme is: Focused on What Matters: Supporting Our Older Adults. 
 
*Koeck shared that the Senior Center will participate in Main Street Trick or Treat on Saturday, October 
24, 2026, from noon to 3:00 pm. Board members were asked to assist with stuffing goodie bags and/or 
distributing the goodie bags. 
 
OLD BUSINESS:  Amanda Koeck 
*Koeck reported that Board members Goodwin, Byrne, Craigen, Padovano, and Rev. Belmer still await 
their reappointment to the Council on Aging. 
 
NEW BUSINESS:  None 
 
COMMUNICATION:  None 
 
BOARD COMMENT: 
*Zichelle thanked Koeck for her support of the successful lunch program offered at The Armory Cafe. 
Thank you and congratulations to Dana Jones on the first anniversary of his appointment as Kitchen 
Coordinator. Zichelle volunteers in The Armory Cafe and shared that Jones is doing a remarkable job and 
the volunteers are pleased with the lunch program and the ease of volunteering in the kitchen. 
 
NEXT MEETING:  Thursday, November 12, 2026 at 1:00 pm 
 
ADJOURNMENT:  Byrne motioned to adjourn and Donohue seconded his motion. No discussion followed 
and there was a unanimous vote to adjourn at 2:20 pm. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
Debbie Dion 
Recording Secretary
